fields.meta_title: Wholesale Order Form Builder for Brands | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a wholesale order form that sells in whole cases, applies price breaks by quantity, and checks each order minimum. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Wholesale Order Form That Applies Your Trade Terms
fields.hero_description: Build a wholesale order form that sells by the case, applies price breaks, and checks each retailer's order minimum.
fields.features_heading: Trade Terms the Form Applies as Retailers Type
fields.features_subheading: A wholesale order form sets what a retailer can order and at what price. This one checks every order before it reaches you.
fields.feature_1:
Quantities that come in whole cases

Set the case size for each product, such as 12 bottles or 6 jars. The quantity box then steps in whole cases, so nobody can order 30 of something you only ship in twelves.
fields.feature_2:
Price breaks shown as the retailer types

Give each product its quantity tiers. The unit price and line total update with every change, and the form says when a few more units would reach the next, cheaper tier.
fields.feature_3:
Reorders that start from the last order

A returning retailer enters an account number, and the form fills in the products from the last order. They change two quantities and submit instead of finding every item again.
fields.feature_4:
Orders sent to the warehouse and the rep

A submitted order goes to the warehouse by email as a pick list. At the same moment, the account's sales rep gets a Slack message with the retailer's name and the order total.
fields.feature_5:
Order history in a database you own

Every order is saved to a database you own, one row per product line, with no cap on how many orders arrive. Sort by retailer to find accounts that have not reordered since spring.
fields.feature_6:
The full code, exported to GitHub

On paid plans, export the full code of the form and its order database to your GitHub repository. A developer can host it on your own servers or keep building on it there.

fields.hero_prompt: Build a wholesale order form for my hot sauce brand that sells bottles in cases of 12 and emails each order to the warehouse.

faq_plan.q: What is a wholesale order form?
How do I create a wholesale order form?

plan.angle: The top 10 for this term is printable PDF sheets, store plugins and a template gallery: a grid of products and blank quantity boxes that leaves the trade terms for someone to check by hand. This page shows a wholesale order form that applies those terms while the retailer fills it in: quantities in whole case packs for a hot sauce brand, an opening-order minimum for a candle maker, price breaks by quantity for a soap maker, and retailer inquiries that reach the sales lead for a leather goods brand. The FAQ covers the definition, building one, what a template should hold, bulk versus wholesale, inquiries, free options, product photos, reorders, private prices and perishable goods.
tab_stories: Emberlow Hot Sauce sells 5 oz bottles in cases of 12, so when Tamsin Achterberg of Fennick Street Market types 30 bottles, the form offers 24 or 36 and she orders 36, 3 full cases at $4.25 a bottle, $153.00.

Brackenfold Candle Co. sets a $250 minimum on a first order and $150 on reorders, so Odile Varga's first order for Marrowby Gifts shows $38 short at $212 until she adds 3 candles at $14 and submits $254.

Corvane Soapworks charges $6.00 a bar under 48, $5.40 from 48 and $4.80 from 96, so when Ines Margulies of Halloway Day Spa enters 90 bars for $486.00, the form shows that 96 bars cost $460.80, $25.20 less, and she orders 96.

Thistlecombe Leather sends any wholesale inquiry expecting more than $1,000 a month to its sales lead Rafferty Osei by direct message in Slack, and the rest wait for the weekly review, so Kestrelvine Outfitters, expecting $1,800 a month, is approved the same day and gets the order form link.
